subject: Affirmation of output rights & subprocessor export-lane checklist
messages:
From: Samuel Green <samuel.green@oakbridgehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Affirmation of output rights & subprocessor export-lane checklist

Hi David,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement / security review we need explicit, contractual confirmation on two related points before we proceed to legal redlines:

1) Non-training / model-improvement: OakBridge needs a commitment that customer content (API payloads, prompts, attachments, transcripts) will not be used to further train or adapt Redwood models. If some data is used for quality/debug purposes, we need a clear operational boundary and an opt-in flow.

2) Output ownership & derivatives: we need assurance that outputs generated from our prompts are assignable to OakBridge (no downstream derivative claims from Redwood or subprocessors), and that any retention needed for caching/latency does not create derivative rights.

Additionally, please provide the following evidence/artefacts so our InfoSec and Legal teams can triage:
- Current subprocessor inventory with roles and geographic jurisdictions (include any cloud infra or managed services vendors).
- KMS jurisdictions table (where keys live, whether HSM/KMS is customer-provisioned or Redwood-managed).
- A short ops note on how ephemeral KV/prefix caching is bounded and how long (if any) prompt/response artifacts persist.
- SOC 2 or other compliance attestations (summary or link).

We have an internal deadline to decide on a partner short-list by EOD next Monday, so a 3-business-day turnaround would be ideal.

Happy to schedule a 30-min call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Samuel Green
Director, Information Security
OakBridge Health

[signature block]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Green <samuel.green@oakbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affirmation of output rights & subprocessor export-lane checklist

Hi Samuel — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Grace (Product) and Hannah (Legal) to make sure we cover technical and contractual pieces.

Short answers up front:
- Non-training: Redwood offers an explicit operational "model-improvement opt-out" for customers. For Hosted API customers we can (i) disable learning by default on a per-account basis, and (ii) provide an evidence package showing no-model-training telemetry (audit logs + sampling). We'll supply the artifact you requested.
- Output ownership: Redwood does not assert ownership over customer prompts or the responses customers receive. We'll propose contract language that assigns output rights to OakBridge and excludes derivative claims by Redwood or our subprocessors.

Attached for your review: subprocessor_inventory_20280420.csv (current list), kms_jurisdictions_table.pdf (high-level key residency), evidence_manifest_v1.zip (ops notes + sample audit logs). I will follow up with SOC 2 links if you need the full report (we can provide an IAQ redacted copy).

A few clarifying points we should confirm on the call:
- Do you require customer-managed KMS or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable if keys are resident in the US (and we map export controls)?
- Are there particular APAC jurisdictions you want us to exclude for subprocessors? We can also provide an export-lane mapping (which subprocessors handle EU/APAC traffic).

We can have a legal redline back to you by COB Friday if that works; evidence package is attached now.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20280420.csv (csv), kms_jurisdictions_table.pdf (pdf), evidence_manifest_v1.zip (zip)

From: Liz Kennedy <liz.kennedy@oakbridgehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Samuel Green <samuel.green@oakbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2028 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Affirmation of output rights & subprocessor export-lane checklist

David/Sam — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from Legal:

- The proposed non-training language is a good start but we need suggested contract text for (i) an express prohibition on model training using customer content, and (ii) a short carveout that describes acceptable operational telemetry (e.g., anonymized metrics) if necessary. Please include a sample redline we can start from.
- Please confirm whether any fallback or compatibility models are trained on public corpora that could, in practice, expose customer outputs to downstream reuse. We need an explicit statement about how Redwood handles model variants and failover routing so we can avoid a gap in the DPA.
- The subprocessor inventory is helpful; we need confirmation of which subprocessors process non-PII vs. PII content and which subprocessors are subject to cross-border transfers.

I've attached a preliminary redline (redline_DPA_draft.docx) highlighting the clauses we'd like to amend. If you can return an annotated redline by Friday, we can get this into our contract queue next week.

Thanks,
Liz Kennedy
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
OakBridge Health

Attachment: redline_DPA_draft.docx

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affirmation of output rights & subprocessor export-lane checklist

Liz / Sam — appreciate the quick read. Couple of concrete next steps and confirmations below: 

1) Contract language: Hannah has prepared an annotated redline that includes two short clauses we propose adding to the DPA: an explicit "No Model Improvement" clause (customer data will not be used to train or adapt models unless customer expressly opts in via a written addendum) and an "Output Assignment" clause (customer retains exclusive rights to outputs and Redwood and subprocessors waive derivative claims). We'll return the annotated redline via the Drive link below by EOD Friday.

2) Evidence & operational controls: the attached evidence_manifest_v1.zip contains: example audit logs showing no training pipeline initiation for account IDs, a short runbook describing ephemeral KV retention (default TTL = 24 hours unless customer requests shorter), and a subprocessor mapping that marks which subprocessors touch PII vs non-PII. Where particular subprocessors have cross-border roles we've indicated the export lane (EU->US, APAC->US) in kms_jurisdictions_table.pdf.

3) KMS options: we can offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted API customers we support Redwood-managed KMS with US-only residency; we can explore onshore-only key storage if that's required by OakBridge.

4) Fallback models & routing: Redwood's routing policy ensures customer traffic is routed to compatible model variants we operate; none of our fallback/compat models will ingest customer data into training pipelines without the opt-in described above. We'll put a short technical note into the evidence pack that spells this out.

Action: I'll upload the annotated DPA redline to the shared Drive and ping you when it's ready. Would you like to schedule a 30-min legal + security sync on Friday to close open points?

Drive (evidence + redline): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_evidence_pack
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/OBH-2028-447

Best,
David Kim
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
